source_title: L’IA au service des Français — Progrès, souveraineté, vigilance
exact_quote: Au total, le programme représente un effort brut d’environ 23 milliards d’euros sur le quinquennat.

corrections.correct: The written plan gives €23 billion gross over five years for the whole plan, including about €11.6 billion in new AI-specific investment. The €5 billion figure covers the public-administration program.
corrections.evidence: The 56-page plan gives the administration figure on PDF page 28 and the overall figures on page 45. Retailleau separately estimated about €25 billion over five years in his July 7 interview: https://republicains.fr/actualites/2026/07/07/sur-lia-nous-avons-une-fenetre-de-tir-de-deux-ans/

corrections.correct: Marianne is the proposed single administrative assistant for the public. Civil servants would receive secure AI assistants. Retailleau proposed redeploying 125,000 staff and leaving 125,000 retirements unfilled.
corrections.evidence: The plan distinguishes the public-facing service from the tools for staff and separates redeployments from vacancies left unfilled.

not_confirmed: The exact July publication day of the PDF.
Acteurs Publics’ precise characterization of the €5 billion figure; its article returned no readable text.
notes: The plan explicitly links sovereign data-center capacity to France’s low-carbon nuclear fleet and prioritizes sites near existing nuclear plants.

source_title: John James says no new data centers until plan to protect communities
exact_quote: No new data centers until we have a plan to protect our communities.

corrections.evidence: WNEM interviewed James at the October 29 campaign stop and gives a local publication time of 8:27 p.m. EDT that day. October 30 appears in the URL.

not_confirmed: James using the exact phrase “five-part moratorium.”
notes: In the station’s firsthand interview, James identified five concerns: local control, water, electricity bills, pollution and prioritizing brownfields over productive farmland.

source_title: Rogers Applauds White House AI Framework That Establishes Global Leadership and Protects Kids Online
exact_quote: by setting a consistent, national framework, which will supercharge innovation, add safeguards to protect kids online, shield communities from higher electric bills

corrections.correct: Rogers endorsed the White House framework on March 20. Michigan Advance published his separate statement about Michigan jobs, investment, safety and data privacy on March 27.
corrections.evidence: The March 27 report identifies the statement as supplied directly to its newsroom and reproduces the complete quotation, including the disputed safety-and-data-privacy clause. https://michiganadvance.com/2026/03/27/mallory-mcmorrow-releases-plan-for-michigan-data-centers-done-right-with-a-focus-on-green-energy/

not_confirmed: A direct statement by Rogers specifying faster permits for new AI facilities; Michigan Advance reports that position in the journalist’s words.
Repeated advocacy across multiple months, beyond the documented March statements.
notes: Both documented statements predate August 20, and the state-investment quotation came from a different statement than the national-framework endorsement.

source_title: An Act Eliminating Certain Tax Incentives for Data Centers — SB 245 bill history
exact_quote: 03-23-2026 FAVORABLE CHANGE OF REFERENCE, SENATE TO COMMITTEE ON Finance, Revenue and Bonding Committee

corrections.correct: March 23 was the last recorded action, referral to Finance, Revenue and Bonding. May 6 was the end of the regular session.
corrections.evidence: The legislative history records the initial Energy and Technology referral on February 19 and both chambers’ Finance referrals on March 23. The bill died without a recorded rejection vote.

notes: The raised bill would have stopped new applications beginning July 1, 2026, while preserving existing agreements under the 2021 sales, use and property tax program, which allowed qualifying agreements of up to 30 years. https://www.cga.ct.gov/2026/TOB/S/PDF/2026SB-00245-R01-SB.PDF

source_title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 July 2026 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
exact_quote: placed on the market before 2 August 2026 shall take the necessary steps in order to comply with Article 50(2) by 2 December 2026.

corrections.correct: Some transparency duties changed. Providers of covered synthetic-content systems already on the market before August 2, 2026 have until December 2, 2026 to comply with Article 50(2).
corrections.evidence: Amending Article 1(39) adds the transition to AI Act Article 111. It expressly includes general-purpose AI systems that generate synthetic content. The separate Chapter V timetable for general-purpose AI models remains in place.

corrections.field: adoption, entry into force and application
corrections.correct: The Council gave final approval June 29. The regulation is dated July 8 and entered into force July 27. The new prohibitions apply from December 2, 2026.
corrections.evidence: Amending Article 1(40) sets the application date for the new prohibitions. The Commission confirms entry into force: https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force

notes: The regulation confirms the December 2, 2027 deadline for Annex III high-risk systems, August 2, 2028 for Annex I product systems, the prohibitions concerning nonconsensual intimate material and child sexual abuse material, and simplifications for smaller firms.

source_title: Proposition de loi visant à encadrer l’implantation des centres de données sur le territoire français
exact_quote: Proposition de loi, adoptée par le Sénat, visant à encadrer l’implantation des centres de données sur le territoire français, n° 2584, déposée le jeudi 26 mars 2026.
notes: David Ros’s bill passed the Senate on March 25 and remains at first reading in the Assembly’s Economic Affairs Committee, with no later examination recorded; the Senate text retains the local planning provisions, and the separate May 26 law already allows qualifying centers to receive the major-national-interest designation. https://www.ecologie.gouv.fr/politiques-publiques/loi-simplification-vie-economique-sve-mesures-urbanisme-construction

source_title: Présidentielle 2027 : Face au risque du pire, je retire ma candidature
exact_quote: Face au risque du pire, je retire ma candidature

corrections.evidence: Ruffin announced his withdrawal himself. His presidential campaign fundraising page identifies the Debout organization: https://don.debout.fr/ruffin2027/

source_title: Leader Schumer Floor Remarks Urging Senate Republicans To Join Democrats To Take Real Action On AI
exact_quote: Senate Democrats want to make it mandatory for data centers to cover their own costs by law

corrections.correct: Schumer explicitly called for mandatory cost coverage on September 30. His postelection remarks about the next Congress were on November 5. Reuters reported them November 6.
corrections.evidence: The event organizer dates Schumer’s keynote to November 5: https://www.americanprogressaction.org/session/keynote-remarks-5/

not_confirmed: A commitment by Democrats to forgo binding limits on AI deployment or energy use.
A primary transcript of the November 5 passage about electricity bills; the organizer’s page identifies the speaker and date but does not transcribe that passage.
notes: Reuters directly attributes the next-Congress cost priority to Schumer; his September remarks establish that he wanted cost coverage to be enforceable, while leaving the question of deployment or energy-use caps open. https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/democrats-planning-flood-ai-bills-when-they-take-control-congress-2026-11-06/

exact_quote: Led by DOL, leverage available discretionary funding, where appropriate, to fund rapid retraining for individuals impacted by AI-related job displacement.

corrections.correct: The plan recommends using available discretionary funds for rapid retraining and establishing an AI Workforce Research Hub under the Department of Labor.
corrections.evidence: Both items appear under “Recommended Policy Actions” in the section headed “Empower American Workers in the Age of AI.”

not_confirmed: An appropriation or disbursement made by the plan itself.
Establishment of an operating hub on the release date.
notes: The July 23 White House release confirms the publication date. https://www.whitehouse.gov/releases/2025/07/white-house-unveils-americas-ai-action-plan/
